basis: Defective hepatic bile-acid uptake defines NTCP deficiency; osteopenia occurs in 3/8 patients, supporting skeletal involvement.
Dementia, parkinsonism and substantia nigra gliosis define a neurodegenerative disease.
Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis is a cutaneous keratinization disorder.
Primary skeletal myopathy; cardiac disease and respiratory insufficiency vary by subtype and are not established in at least 30% across this umbrella.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia and hydrocephalus define it; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Respiratory failure reflects thoracic restriction without documented intrinsic lung damage.
Bone fragility, osteopenia and vertebral deformity define OI11. Blue sclerae do not establish ocular damage; dentinogenesis imperfecta occurs in only 3/22.
Developmental and intellectual impairment are frequent; hearing loss and aural atresia are described as common defining features. Hypothyroidism is occasional (5-29%).
Rhizomelia 3/6 and hypothyroidism 3/4; cardiac defects and hearing impairment each 2/5. Epidermoid cysts 2/5 omitted at cap; intellectual disability only 1/4 in broader reporting.
Monogenic diabetes defines this concept; diabetic end-organ complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Premature fusion of both lambdoid skull sutures; no common direct neurologic or ocular damage is established.
Carcinoma originates in a salivary gland, usually the parotid; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited adrenal cortisol deficiency; neurologic injury is reported in a singleton, and achalasia/alacrima in 1/2 each, insufficient to establish common involvement across GCCD2.
Histologic umbrella dominated by breast fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumors, outside the axes; renal origin belongs to a specific minority subtype.
Carcinoma arises in the gastric pylorus.
Destructive xanthogranulomatous inflammation of a salivary gland; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not established by this concept.
IGF-I resistance is endocrine; intellectual disability/microcephaly and skeletal deformities occur in 30-79%, with delayed skeletal maturation in 80-99%.
Inherited glomerular disease causes progressive renal failure; reduced visual acuity occurs in 8/8, retinal detachment in 5/9 and pigmentary retinopathy in 3/9.
Persistent systemic arterial hypertension defines the disease; hypertensive renal, retinal and cardiac complications are separately diagnosed.
Sensorineural deafness and missing teeth define the syndrome; vestibular dysfunction is covered by the otologic axis.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm flagella and infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Progressive skeletal muscle dystrophy with weakness, atrophy and contractures; reduced reflexes do not establish a separate peripheral neuropathy.
Axonal motor-sensory neuropathy defines CMT2; chronic denervation causes distal skeletal muscle wasting and deformity in most clinically affected patients.
Inherited polycystic liver disease; the definition does not establish common renal or other extrahepatic involvement.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability defines this concept; the broad carbohydrate-transport ancestor alone does not establish a metabolic disease.
Tumor originates in the mediastinum, which has no specified axis; lung, airway, pleural or cardiovascular invasion is not established.
